U BGRAP H − W EIGHT : Given a graph G whose vertices and edges have as- sociated integer weights, and an integer k, does G contain a subgraph of weight k? (Define the weight of a graph to be the sum of the weights of the vertices and edges of that graph.)  prove this is NP-Complete

message.content: This problem is in NP because verifying a subgraph takes polynomial time. We can reduce the Subset Sum Problem to it easily here. The reduction maps elements to vertices with specific integer weight values assigned. Edges connect all pairs to allow any subset selection within the structure. A solution exists if and only if some combination sums exactly to target k. Therefore, this decision problem is indeed NP-Complete by standard computational complexity theory principles.
